memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses answered the people, 'Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the
deliverance the LORD will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today you will
never see again.'" - Ex 14:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses does not argue with their accusations. He points them somewhere else.

Three commands: do not be afraid, stand firm, and see. Notice what is absent.
There is no strategy, no call to arms, no plan of escape. Their entire assignment
is to stay where they are and watch.

That is much harder than it sounds. Everything in us wants to do something when
we are frightened. Doing something feels like control. Standing still feels like
giving up.

But some situations are beyond our ability to fix, and in those moments the
instruction is to stand and let God act. Not passivity born of laziness, but
stillness born of trust. Psalm 46:10 says, "Be still, and know that I am God."

Then Moses adds a promise: "The Egyptians you see today you will never see
again." What terrified them at breakfast would be gone by nightfall.

Sometimes the thing looming over you has a shorter life than you think. It looks
permanent from where you stand. God sees its final day.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you trying to fix something God is asking you to stand still in?
2. What feels permanent right now that God may already have an end date for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, teach me when to act and when to stand still and watch You work. Quiet my
need to control what only You can handle. Amen.
